title: Plans — round 7: the changes you asked for, and the assistant stepping in

steps.path: A ChatGPT plan waiting for approval
steps.headline: Approximate limits now show a ~ in front of the number, and the extra sentence is gone.
steps.changed: "Up to about 42,000 tokens" plus a warning line became "Up to ~42,000 tokens", as you asked.
steps.notice: A shorter card; the ~ says the limit is approximate.
steps.risk: Someone who doesn't know what ~ means gets no explanation.

steps.headline: Approve is now on the right, with Comment to its left.
steps.changed: The two buttons swapped places and moved to the right edge, following your new rule for filled buttons, now written into the design guide.
steps.notice: The main action sits where the app's other dialogs put it.
steps.risk: If you're used to the old spot, you may reach left for Approve once.

steps.path: The dot on a conversation's tab while a specialist waits for your answer
steps.headline: A specialist waiting on you now lights the conversation's red dot and plays the alert sound.
steps.changed: This now happens for ordinary specialists and plan specialists alike, the same way it does when the assistant itself asks.
steps.notice: You notice a waiting question even from another conversation.
steps.risk: More alerts during busy plans with several specialists.

steps.path: Specialists button while a plan runs
steps.headline: The Specialists popup lists a running plan as one line you can open.
steps.changed: Each plan is a single row with its name and where it is ("step 1 of 3", matching the card). Ordinary specialists are listed as before.
steps.notice: You can see a plan is running without scrolling to its card.

steps.headline: Opening a plan's row shows the specialists working on it.
steps.changed: Each specialist appears with the same controls ordinary ones have (Note, Stop). A plan with a waiting question opens by itself.
steps.notice: You can check on or stop one specialist without finding the card.
steps.risk: The popup gets long while a big plan runs.

steps.path: A plan that ran out of budget, just after it paused
steps.headline: When a plan needs a decision, the card greys out while the assistant looks into it.
steps.changed: The card is dimmed with no buttons and says "The assistant is looking into this." Below it, a collapsed "Note for the assistant" row shows what the assistant was told.
steps.notice: You don't have to work out what went wrong yourself.
steps.risk: The assistant's look costs a normal reply's worth of usage.

steps.path: After the assistant suggests adding budget, with Add budget pressed
steps.headline: The assistant explains the problem and the card comes back with its suggested amount ready.
steps.changed: The card shows "The assistant suggests: …" and Add budget opens pre-filled with the suggested 15,000 tokens. Nothing is added until you press Continue.
steps.notice: One click from the recommendation to a running plan, and you still decide.
steps.risk: It's easy to accept the suggested amount without reading why.

steps.path: After the assistant suggests trying again
steps.headline: When trying again makes sense, the assistant says why and Continue is the main button.
steps.changed: Stop is the light button on the left and Continue the filled one on the right.
steps.notice: The card tells you whether it's worth continuing.

steps.headline: When continuing wouldn't help, the assistant recommends stopping and the card offers only Stop.
steps.changed: One filled Stop button, with the assistant's reason above it; it may also propose a revised plan below.
steps.notice: No buttons that would just fail again.

steps.path: Repeating steps that never met their goal, after the assistant replied in chat
steps.headline: If the assistant only answers in chat, the card comes back with its normal buttons.
steps.changed: For repeated steps that never met their goal that is Stop only; the assistant's reply below explains what to do instead.
steps.notice: The card never stays greyed out.

steps.path: A priced ChatGPT plan's limit line
steps.headline: Should approximate dollar amounts also use the ~ ("~$0.12") instead of "about $0.12"?
steps.today: The builder put a ~ in front of dollar amounts too, so a ChatGPT plan's limit line reads "Up to ~$0.12". You asked for the ~ on the usage numbers only.
steps.problem: Mixing "about" and "~" in one line reads inconsistently, but you only asked about the usage numbers.
steps.proposal: Pick one style for dollar amounts.

pros: Same style as the usage numbers.
cons: "~" before a dollar sign is less familiar to some people.

steps.path: The collapsed "Note for the assistant" row under a greyed-out plan card
steps.headline: Should the note the app sends the assistant stay visible in the chat as a collapsed row?
steps.today: When a plan is handed to the assistant, the app sends it a short note about what happened. That note shows in the chat as a collapsed "Note for the assistant" row you can open.
steps.problem: It's honest about what the assistant was told, but it's one more line in the chat.
steps.proposal: Keep it visible and collapsed, or hide it.

options.label: Keep it, collapsed
pros: You can always see what the assistant was told.

options.label: Hide it
cons: The assistant's reply can look like it came from nowhere.
